images.caption: This map shows the footprint of the 2024 Park Fire, which has burned more than 390,000 acres in Butte and Tehama counties in Northern California. The fire, which is the fifth largest in California state history, was caused by arson. It has destroyed at least 437 structures but has caused no fatalities. This map was made in QGIS using data from the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire), the United States Geological Survey, OpenStreetMap, and others.

images.filename: Burned area along Cohasset Road after the Park Fire (2024)-L1006013.jpg
images.caption: A burned area along Cohasset Road north of Chico, California, after the Park Fire. On the night of July 24, 2024, the Park Fire exploded and swept into Cohasset. The Park Fire is the fourth largest in California history, and the largest ever caused by arson in the state.
images.alt: A burned area along Cohasset Road north of Chico, California, after the Park Fire. On the night of July 24, 2024, the Park Fire exploded and swept into Cohasset. The Park Fire is the fourth largest in California history, and the largest ever caused by arson in the state.
